memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then to the place the Lord your God will choose as a dwelling for his Name—there you are to bring everything I command you: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and special gifts, and all the choice possessions you have vowed to the Lord. And there rejoice before the Lord your God—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levites from your towns, who have no allotment or inheritance of their own. - Deut 12:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Israel came to worship, they were to bring their offerings — and notice the phrase "all the choice possessions you have vowed to the Lord." God's people were to bring their best to Him, not their leftovers. Worship involved giving, and the giving was to be generous and wholehearted. And once again, joy fills the scene: they were to "rejoice before the Lord," including even the Levites who had no land of their own. Worship was to be generous, joyful, and inclusive of all.

There is a heart-check here about what we bring to God. Do we give Him our best — our best time, energy, resources, attention — or only what is left over after everything else has taken its share? The people were called to bring their "choice possessions," reflecting a heart that treasured God enough to give Him the first and the finest. Half-hearted, leftover worship reveals a half-hearted heart.

We give our best to God not to earn His love, but because He has first given His best to us. "God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son" (John 3:16). The Father held nothing back; He gave the most precious gift of all. In response, we bring Him our best — cheerfully, for "God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Cor 9:7). This includes our generosity toward others, especially those in need, just as the Levites were included in the celebration. What are you bringing to God? Offer Him your best today, with a joyful and generous heart, in grateful response to the One who gave everything for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I bring God my best, or only my leftovers?
- How does remembering God's gift of His Son shape my generosity?
- Who might God be calling me to include in His blessing, as the Levites were included?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You gave Your very best in Jesus, holding nothing back. In response, help me bring You my best — my time, my resources, my whole heart — with joy and generosity. Make me a cheerful giver who reflects Your generous love to others. Amen.
